issues.description: Default turn_detection_mode change from EXTERNAL to FIXED is a silent breaking change
issues.detail: Existing users who relied on the default value will get different endpointing behavior after upgrade. The PR is labeled as a feature/fix but this is effectively a behavior change at the default level. Should be called out as a breaking change in the changelog (or in a migration note) rather than only in a 'fixed' bullet, and ideally a deprecation cycle considered.

issues.description: Warning log fires for VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame in ADAPTIVE/SMART_TURN modes during normal operation
issues.detail: When _enable_vad is True (ADAPTIVE/SMART_TURN), receiving a VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame from Pipecat's VAD now logs a warning every turn. If a pipeline upstream of this service uses Pipecat VAD (common), this will spam warning logs in normal use. Either downgrade to debug, or only warn when this combination is genuinely misconfigured.

issues.description: speech_segment_config is unconditionally overwritten even when user didn't set split_sentences
issues.detail: `config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=params.split_sentences or False)` always assigns, even when params.split_sentences is None. If the underlying VoiceAgentConfig had a different default or pre-set value for speech_segment_config, this silently overrides it to emit_sentences=False. Either guard with `if params.split_sentences is not None:` or document that this resets the config.

The name FIXED reads like 'fixed-window endpointing performed by the STT engine,' but per the PR description it actually means 'Pipecat controls end-of-turn.' Both FIXED and EXTERNAL now disable internal VAD and rely on Pipecat-emitted frames; the only behavioral difference between them in this diff is which frame triggers finalize. Consider clearer naming (e.g., PIPECAT_VAD vs PIPECAT_TURN) or expand the docstring to disambiguate.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics call moved but not removed
issues.detail: `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` was simply repositioned within `_handle_start_of_turn`. Dead/commented code should either be deleted or activated; leaving it in suggests unfinished work and accumulates over time.

issues.description: EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED is referenced but not shown to exist in this diff
issues.detail: `self._enable_vad` now checks against `EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED`, which is a Speechmatics SDK enum value. The diff doesn't show whether FIXED exists in the pinned `0.0.99+` SDK. If the SDK doesn't have it, this AttributeError will fire at import/init time. Reviewer should verify the SDK exposes EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED at the floor version.

issues.description: Class-level TurnDetectionMode docstring still confusing about which mode is which
issues.detail: The updated docstring says 'If using Pipecat's built-in endpointing, then use TurnDetectionMode.FIXED (default).' But EXTERNAL also uses Pipecat-side endpointing in the new model. Docstring should distinguish FIXED vs EXTERNAL clearly so users know which to pick.

issues.description: PR description does not mention split_sentences but changelog does
issues.detail: The 'What's Changed' section omits the split_sentences addition that appears in `changelog/3328.added.md`. Minor documentation drift; add a bullet to the PR body for reviewer scannability.

issues.description: No tests added for new behavior
issues.detail: The diff adds a new TurnDetectionMode value, changes the default, switches frame listener type, and adds split_sentences plumbing — none accompanied by tests. STT services tend to be hard to unit test, but at minimum a test verifying _enable_vad mapping and process_frame routing for VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame in each mode would protect against regressions.

dissents.topic: Is the default change from EXTERNAL to FIXED breaking?

positions.position: Changing the default endpointing mode silently alters runtime behavior for every existing user who didn't pin the value. This is a breaking change and warrants a major-version bump or at least a migration note.

Pipecat is pre-1.0-style and the SDK floor was just raised to 0.0.99. The previous default produced bugs (no finalize on VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame); calling the new default 'fixed' is a correction, not a break, and the changelog entry is sufficient.

dissents.topic: Should the warning on VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame in VAD-enabled modes be a warning or debug?

positions.position: If both Pipecat VAD and Speechmatics internal VAD are running, that's a real misconfiguration deserving a warning so users notice and fix their pipeline.

VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame is emitted by Pipecat's standard VAD processor and is routinely present in pipelines regardless of STT-internal VAD. Warning per-turn becomes noise; debug or one-shot warning is appropriate.
Always setting the config makes the service's behavior deterministic and independent of SDK defaults that may drift across versions.
Overwriting a structured sub-config when the user didn't ask is surprising; guard with `is not None` so users can rely on SDK defaults or set it via other code paths.

review.summary: The PR is a focused fix that aligns SpeechmaticsSTTService with Speechmatics SDK 0.0.99+, adds a new FIXED turn detection mode that defers endpointing to Pipecat, listens to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame for finalize, and plumbs through a split_sentences option. The core direction is sound and the changelog entries describe the behavior change. However, the default change from EXTERNAL to FIXED is effectively a behavior change for existing users and deserves louder migration framing. The warning log on VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame in ADAPTIVE/SMART_TURN modes will fire during normal pipeline operation and should be downgraded or scoped. speech_segment_config is now overwritten unconditionally, which can mask user-side or SDK-side defaults. No tests accompany the change, and FIXED naming overlaps semantically with EXTERNAL in a way the docstring doesn't fully disambiguate.
